tasks.short: Sell merchandise and arrange delivery, insurance, financing or service contracts.

steps.what: Discuss the purchase, budget, delivery needs and optional services.
Check merchandise prices, delivery availability and approved service options.
Submit requested financing or insurance details and receive the provider's response.
Prepare the bundled quote and required contract documents.
Explain costs and obligations, answer questions and obtain the customer's acceptance.
Record the accepted sale and authorize selected delivery and service arrangements.
Send approved arrangements to fulfillment teams and confirm them to the customer.

tasks.design: A reusable quote generator combines approved exports from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} with contract templates in the {DOCS}; live connectors can replace exports later. Configure the {PARTNER_PORTAL} application flow and an approval in the {WORKFLOW}, then send confirmations through the {EMAIL} only for accepted orders. The salesperson explains commitments, while the external provider retains financing and insurance decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices, delivery capacity and provider forms sit in separate systems. Commercial terms and disclosure requirements vary by retailer and provider.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and approval features handle much of the flow. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining connectors and document assembly cheaper to build, without changing provider permissions.
tasks.still_hard: Live slot reservations, provider access and changing contract terms need reliable interfaces. Financing and insurance advice permissions depend on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Understand affordability concerns, explain obligations clearly and recognize when an optional service is unsuitable.

ambition.what: Compare delivery and service bundle prices during the sales conversation.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less copying and more time explaining purchase choices. The salesperson can compare approved bundles immediately; credit, insurance and discount authority do not expand.

reach.task: Resolve delivery requests that lack a confirmed slot.
reach.learn: Reservation expiry, fulfillment cutoffs and the difference between a requested and confirmed delivery.

reach.task: Evaluate the contribution margin of service bundles.
reach.learn: Service costs, cancellation exposure and approved pricing limits.

evidence.claim: Approved prices, templates and order fields can support deterministic quote assembly.
Provider submissions can be simplified where existing forms support prefill and controlled submission.
The proposed integration and time reductions are estimates, not documented results for this task.

assumptions: This describes a retailer offering at least some delivery, financing, insurance or service options; each purchase follows only relevant branches.
The salesperson's time includes assisting the application, not the provider's underwriting work or passive waiting.
The communication-heavy priors remain appropriate; paperwork and coordination are more structured than the whole task.
Customer authorization is obtained before transmitting application details. Provider decisions remain outside this automation.
EU GDPR and AI Act requirements apply. National rules determine advice permissions and any employee consultation.
Build ranges cover one store workflow and a small number of providers, including access and consultation where required.
No separate approval is needed for confirmations that exactly reproduce an already approved order.
unknowns: Which optional services are offered and who may explain or recommend them?
Do provider agreements permit prefill, exports or integration?
Which system holds authoritative prices and delivery reservations?
Which approvals are required for discounts, contract changes and customer applications?
What customer data may be retained, and for how long?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed workflow?
research_questions: Which current modules already generate quotes and contract packs?
Can delivery slots be reserved atomically while an order is approved?
Can provider forms reuse customer-entered details without creating another sensitive-data store?
new_work: Handle rejected applications, expired slots and incomplete provider responses.
Maintain approved terms, prices and contract templates.
Monitor failed confirmations and connector changes.

tasks.short: Estimate merchandise quantities and prices for a customer's project.

steps.what: Discuss the project and collect dimensions, surfaces, layout and desired finish.
Read product specifications and record coverage, pack sizes and application requirements.

loop.input: Selected product specifications with document versions and the project brief.
loop.output: Coverage, units, pack sizes and application requirements, each linked to a source passage.
loop.check: Validate units and numeric source matches; the salesperson approves new or changed parameters before use.
loop.stop: At most five documents and two extraction attempts per product; missing or conflicting values go to manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier specifications use varied prose and tables. Use structured catalogue fields instead wherever available.

steps.what: Calculate areas, coverage, waste allowances and rounded purchase quantities.
Check uncertain surfaces, awkward layouts and whether measurements need professional verification.
Price quantities using current prices and prepare the sales quote.
Review the estimate, explain assumptions and release the quote to the customer.

tasks.design: A reusable calculator on the {WORKFLOW} applies explicit measurement, coverage, waste and pack-rounding rules, then requests current prices from the {ERP}. A bounded extraction loop reads irregular specifications from the {DOCS}; reviewed parameters are stored for reuse, and structured catalogue fields bypass the loop. The salesperson checks project uncertainties and approves the customer quote.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project inputs vary, supplier documents use different formats and estimate rules often live in personal worksheets. Connecting those rules to current prices previously required bespoke work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building calculators, validation and quote templates. Bounded document extraction can reduce transcription without replacing measurement or material judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Poor measurements, unusual room geometry and hidden surface conditions remain costly sources of error. Different materials need different calculation rules.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a neat calculation rests on unreliable measurements or unsuitable material assumptions.

ambition.what: A side-by-side material and waste scenario estimate while the customer waits.

tasks.altitude: The salesperson spends less time calculating and can compare two realistic project choices in one visit. They gain no installation or surveying authority; uncertain projects still need specialist verification.

reach.role: sales representative of technical and scientific products
reach.task: Check whether a proposed material meets the customer's application requirements.
reach.learn: Coverage conditions, substrate compatibility and the limits of manufacturer specifications.

reach.task: Convert a quantity estimate into orderable packs and accessories.
reach.learn: Pack rounding, batch availability and required companion items.

evidence.claim: Area, coverage, pack rounding and price calculations can use deterministic rules once inputs are confirmed.
A bounded extraction loop can propose specification fields with source passages for human checking.
The digest provides no documented case for this project-estimation workflow or its projected time savings.

assumptions: This describes a project-based retailer selling products such as paint or flooring.
A {SPREADSHEET} calculation is a typical bridge here; retailers with an existing estimator should configure it first.
The situational-input prior remains valid. Once measurements and material assumptions are confirmed, arithmetic has higher rule coverage.
The physical customer conversation is preserved; the main reduction comes from calculation and quote preparation.
The starter covers one material family. Further families require separate rules and verification.
Employee review time includes checking extracted parameters; customers' measurement work is outside the time shares.
EU GDPR and AI Act requirements apply where customer information or model processing is involved. National rules determine any consultation.
Build ranges are planning estimates for a reusable starter, including access and consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Which product families, units and waste rules are used?
Does an existing estimator already handle these calculations?
Are specifications available as structured fields or only documents?
Who verifies customer measurements and approves material suitability?
Which quotes are indicative and which create a binding commitment?
Can current prices and stock be accessed through approved exports or interfaces?
research_questions: Which material families can share calculation rules without hiding important differences?
How accurately can extraction recover coverage conditions as well as numeric coverage values?
Which historical estimate errors came from arithmetic rather than incorrect project assumptions?
new_work: Approve new or changed specification parameters.
Maintain material rules, units and pack sizes.
Handle missing measurements and conflicting specifications.
Check calculator changes against representative projects.
Retire stale specification versions and price feeds.

tasks.short: Rent merchandise, explain its use, and record handover and return.

steps.what: Discuss the intended use, rental period and customer's experience.
Check rental records in {OTHER} for availability, rates and item history.
Select a suitable item and inspect its condition and accessories.
Prepare rental terms, explain charges and obtain the customer's agreement.
Take the rental payment or deposit through the till system in {OTHER}.
Demonstrate safe use, confirm understanding and hand over the item.
Update rental records in {OTHER} with the item, customer and return deadline.
Inspect the returned item, check accessories and discuss reported faults.
Close the rental in {OTHER}, settle charges and release any remaining deposit.

tasks.design: Configure rental records in the {OTHER} rental system for availability, agreements, item identifiers and barcode handover and return events. Connect the {OTHER} till system where supported so payment status and approved settlements update the rental record without re-entry. The salesperson retains suitability checks, demonstrations, condition inspections and approval of customer charges.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rental records, till payments and physical condition checks are separate. Some retailers have only partly configured their existing rental software.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing rental software already supports availability, item history and barcode events. A small connector can remove repeated payment and status entry.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, customer competence and disputed damage remain human work. Concurrent bookings and deposit handling require reliable transaction controls.
tasks.human_edge: Judge suitability, demonstrate safe use and resolve disagreement about returned condition.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less record entry and more time for demonstrations and difficult returns. Decision rights remain unchanged, including approval limits for charges and deposit releases.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Resolve disputed damage charges and unavailable-item substitutions.
reach.learn: Condition evidence, charging limits and maintenance quarantine rules.

reach.task: Teach customers how to operate unfamiliar rental equipment.
reach.learn: Demonstration structure and practical checks of customer understanding.

evidence.claim: Booqable supports rental availability, item rental history and barcode check-in.
Payment and rental status synchronization depends on the interfaces available in the installed systems.
Physical demonstrations and condition inspections limit how much of the whole task can be automated.

assumptions: The retailer operates a rental counter with existing rental records; {OTHER} covers both rental and till systems as separate categories.
Time shares cover one completed rental lifecycle, including return, and exclude elapsed rental time.
The communication-heavy prior is retained, but availability lookup and records have stronger rule coverage.
Payment automation prepares amounts and updates records; the salesperson approves collection and settlement.
Returned items become available only after a satisfactory inspection. Failed items enter maintenance quarantine.
EU GDPR and AI Act requirements apply. National rules determine retention, consumer terms and any employee consultation.
Build ranges cover configuration and one payment connection, including access and consultation where required.
unknowns: Which rental and till features are already licensed and configured?
Can item identifiers and payment references be shared between systems?
How are reservations protected against concurrent bookings?
Which rentals require identity checks, competence checks or special instructions?
Who may approve damage charges, refunds and deposit releases?
How are cleaning, inspection and maintenance delays reflected in availability?
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove re-entry without adding a separate records app?
Which payment interface supports the retailer's actual deposit and refund process?
Which return events must keep an item unavailable until further inspection?
new_work: Resolve payment synchronization failures and duplicate booking events.
Maintain rental rates, agreement templates and item identifiers.
Review proposed settlements and escalate disputed damage.
Correct missing handover or return events.

tasks.short: Estimate repair or alteration costs and explain the proposed work to the customer.

steps.what: Discuss the fault or alteration and record the customer's desired outcome.
Inspect the merchandise and assess the likely work, parts and labour.
Read approved labour rates, standard operation times and warranty terms.
Look up required part prices and the price of comparable replacement merchandise.
Calculate parts, labour, applicable tax and the resulting repair estimate.
Check scope, uncertainty and whether further diagnosis is needed before quoting.
Prepare the customer quote with scope, exclusions and replacement price.
Explain uncertainty and alternatives, approve the quote and release it to the customer.

tasks.design: A reusable estimate form on the {WORKFLOW} records the technician's assessment, selects approved rates from the {DOCS} and obtains part and replacement prices from the {ERP}. Deterministic calculations produce the service quote and repair-versus-replacement comparison using versioned templates from the {DOCS}. The technician checks scope and uncertainty, and the salesperson approves release; an existing service-estimate module should replace custom code where available.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagnosis is difficult to standardize, so the calculation and document work has often stayed manual too. Rate sheets, part prices and technician notes are separate.
tasks.enabler_now: A structured assessment form separates expert diagnosis from repeatable costing. AI-assisted coding makes the calculator, price connection and templates cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden damage and uncertain labour cannot be resolved by a calculator. Warranty interpretation and commitments about final prices need experienced review.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a credible estimate from a guess and explain when repair is uncertain or uneconomic.

ambition.what: A written repair-versus-replacement comparison with priced options and explicit uncertainties.

tasks.altitude: The salesperson spends less time assembling estimates and more time helping customers choose an option. Diagnosis stays with the qualified person; quote and warranty authority remain within existing limits.

reach.task: Turn an accepted repair quote into a complete service order.
reach.learn: Parts availability, diagnostic prerequisites and customer authorization for additional work.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Review estimates that exceed standard price or warranty limits.
reach.learn: Estimate variance, approval thresholds and the difference between an estimate and a fixed-price commitment.

evidence.claim: Confirmed parts, labour and tax inputs support deterministic estimate calculations.
Structured assessment fields and templates can reduce quote preparation without automating diagnosis.
The digest contains no documented repair-estimation case or measured savings for this design.

assumptions: This describes a retailer offering repairs or alterations through an internal or contracted technician.
The technician may be the salesperson for simple alterations, but the diagnostic decision remains a distinct step.
Shares cover active effort across the service-estimation task, including technician effort; they are not solely salesperson savings.
The judgement-heavy prior remains appropriate for diagnosis. Its low rule coverage does not apply to arithmetic after scope is confirmed.
Replacement comparisons are currently ad hoc; the proposed change adds a consistent written comparison.
Warranty rules are already approved and encoded as explicit conditions. Ambiguous cases are referred for review.
EU GDPR and AI Act requirements apply. National rules determine consumer commitments and any employee consultation.
Build ranges cover one repair or alteration family, including access and consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Which merchandise can be assessed by sales staff and which requires a qualified technician?
Are approved operation times and labour rates available?
Does the existing service system already support estimates and templates?
How reliable are part prices and availability?
Who decides warranty coverage and approves nonstandard prices?
Which quotes bind the retailer to a fixed price?
How often do customers currently receive replacement comparisons?
research_questions: Which estimate errors arise from costing rather than diagnosis?
Can standard operations cover enough repairs to justify configuration before custom development?
Which uncertainty descriptions help customers understand possible additional work without implying a price guarantee?
new_work: Maintain service rates, operation codes and quote templates.
Handle missing part prices and uncertain warranty coverage.
Review scope exceptions before quote release.
Compare accepted estimates with completed-job costs to improve standard operations.
Maintain replacement-product mappings without implying technical equivalence.

role.altitude: Retail salespeople spend less time transferring data and preparing documents, while retaining customer conversations and physical checks. They can present priced alternatives sooner; financial, technical and commercial decision rights expand only through explicit delegation.
reach: Order clerk: prepare complete orders and resolve fulfillment exceptions.
First-line supervisor of retail sales workers: assess disputed charges and nonstandard quotes.
Sales manager: compare bundle margins and commercial outcomes.
Demonstrator and product promoter: teach safe use and check customer understanding.
skills_to_grow: Validate measurements, units, prices and source versions.
Explain estimates, exclusions and contractual commitments plainly.
Use structured forms without losing important customer context.
Recognize when technical or financial judgement requires another qualified role.
Diagnose failed handoffs and distinguish drafts from approved commitments.
role.ambitious_version: Become a project adviser who presents priced purchase, rental, repair and replacement options using reusable calculators and approved data. Start with portable forms and templates; connect company systems as access permits, while keeping diagnosis and regulated decisions with authorized roles.
